notes: Advisory evidence was refreshed at implementation time rather than carried forward: 0.35.4 is still the newest published 0.35.x, so the floor names the current fixed version and not a historical one.

The lockfile also drops a stale "dev": true flag on fsevents. A control test established this is not caused by the change: reconciling the UNMODIFIED package.json removes the same flag, so it is pre-existing drift inherited from PR #48's lockfile. It was kept rather than reverted, because reverting would leave the committed lockfile disagreeing with npm's own deterministic output. It moves one optional darwin-only package from 320 to 321 non-dev entries and the audit remains 0 at every severity.

RISK-002 assessed rather than asserted. The other four overrides entries - postcss, nanoid, deepmerge-ts, mysql2 - each declare a floor below the version currently resolved, which is the same structural property that made the sharp entry dangerous. None of them carries a current production advisory, so none is a vulnerability today; the finding is a latent pattern, not a defect, and UT-005 is what will notice if that changes.

ST-007 is the only test that can fail if this change is absent, because on the current graph every other assertion passes identically before and after. It is deliberately a test that breaks the thing it is proving.
